desc: Parse N, M, K and the graph edges; store edges as (w, u, v).
Run Kruskal (sort edges by weight ascending, DSU) to obtain the MST edges.
Build the Kruskal reconstruction tree: for each added edge of weight w, create a new node with that weight and make the two DSU roots its children; the final root represents the whole set.
On the reconstruction tree, for each node compute `subtree_max` (maximum edge weight in its subtree) and sort children by `subtree_max` descending.
Perform a postorder traversal of the reconstruction tree to obtain a total order `ord` of the original N vertices that makes the ultrametric Monge.
Preprocess the original MST for LCA queries with max-edge-on-path (binary lifting: parent[k][v], maxEdge[k][v], depth).
Map each original vertex to its position in `ord` (rank from 0 to N-1).
Sort the sequence A by the rank of A_i, and sort the sequence B by the rank of B_j.
For i = 0..K-1, compute f(A_sorted[i], B_sorted[i]) using the LCA max-edge query in O(log N).
Sum the K values and print the result.
Run solution on Sample 1 (expect 8) and Sample 2 (expect 3); debug if output mismatches.
Write a brute-force checker for small N (N≤8) and random graphs to compare greedy result against O(K!) optimal matching.
